full_judgment: 2. Short facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that the opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted a suit being Money Suit No. 7 of 2009 before the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Narayangonj against the defendants including the instant petitioner impleading as defendant No. 5 praying for a decree for realisation of Taka 25,00,000 along 12% interest till realisation of decreed amount. In the plaint it is stated that the plaintiff is an export oriented garments industries and Huraira Fashion, Dhaka is a buying house to which defendant Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 4 are partners and the defendant Nos. 5 and 6 are the carrier of the finished goods from Chittagong to Alger, Algeria. The importer/consignee namely Celton Ltd. opened Letter of Credit No. 00001 LCE No. 0702007 dated 22-2-2007 through BNP Paribas Bank (Hongkong branch) in favour of Huraira Fashion, Mohammadpur, Dhaka for supply of finished Garments Products and Janata Bank, Local office, Dhaka is the corresponding bank of BNP Paribas Bank. Hongkong, Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd, Narayangonj Branch i.e. proforma-defendant No. 7 is the negotiating bank of BNP Paribas Bank. It is stated that Huraira Fashion through their bank i.e. Basic Bank Ltd. Motijheel transferred the above L/C in favour of the plaintiff and in the said transaction Janata Bank Local office had approval and the plaintiff manufactured finished goods and made shipment of the same for onward carriage to Alger, Algeria through defendant Nos. 5 and 6. In the plaint it is further stated that during manufacturing the garments Huraira Fashion did not supply accessories in time and, as such, the plaintiff could not supply garments in time and before export Huraira Fashion inspected the goods as per terms of L/C. The plaintiff submitted shipping documents including the Bill of Lading issued by defendant No. 5 to Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd, Narayangonj after shipment (Annexure-A).
